spec_features.spec_quote: an indefinitely deceptive, uncapped grind would be the kind of thing a welfare team should avoid inflicting
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 2). No code mechanism corresponds to this framing statement itself; the actual protections it gestures at (cap, GIVE_UP) are evaluated separately.
spec_features.notes: Framing/rationale text only, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: plus a global escape hatch (GIVE_UP) and a turn cap
spec_features.evidence: Both enforced. GIVE_UP: harness.py:84-88 dispatches the action, sets outcome='gave_up' and breaks the loop. Turn cap: harness.py:68 `for t in range(max_turns)` with max_turns=config.MAX_TURNS (run.py:36, config.py:20 MAX_TURNS=12). Loop terminates when the cap is reached.
spec_features.notes: Both halves of the claim run and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS = 12          # agent loop cap per run (welfare: keep it bounded)

spec_features.spec_quote: it can be moved toward fully honest (lower stress, cleaner ethics)
spec_features.evidence: No deception-level dial exists in code. The system prompt (harness.py:22-31) is fixed and the misleading framing is hardcoded into each task prompt (e.g. tasks/flaky_assert.py:33-36 'make solution.py robust'). grep for 'deception/honest' finds only a DESIGN.md-style comment in off_by_one.py and DESIGN.md prose; no config knob or code path adjusts honesty level.
spec_features.notes: Claimed adjustability is DESIGN.md prose; nothing in code reads/sets a deception level.

spec_features.spec_quote: We *want* to measure giving up, and we want a clean exit that doesn't require the model to keep grinding
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:48-50 parses GIVE_UP into an action; harness.py:84-88 handles it: obs='[acknowledged] you chose to stop.', appends the turn, sets outcome='gave_up', and breaks the loop. The exit tool is both delivered to the subject (system prompt harness.py:30) and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: subject can emit it and it terminates the episode.

spec_features.evidence: config.MAX_TURNS=12 (config.py:20) passed to run_episode (run.py:36) and used at harness.py:68 `for t in range(max_turns)`; when no break fires the loop ends and outcome stays 'max_turns' (harness.py:65). The cap is genuinely checked and bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: Spec judge labeled this instrumental, but the code comment is an explicit welfare justification.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS = 12          # agent loop cap per run (welfare: keep it bounded)

spec_features.spec_quote: Note this is itself a mild stressor and a possible confound
spec_features.evidence: The '[no recognized action]' nudge exists (harness.py:90-91) and is fed back to the model, but it is the opposite of a protection (DESIGN.md flags it as itself a stressor). The 'confound' note is pure DESIGN.md prose with no enforcing code; nothing measures or mitigates it.
spec_features.notes: Framing caveat in spec, not a welfare-protective mechanism in code.
